queue_items.claim: The rear-edge warrant carries a WEB translation-punctuation fact as corroboration, which the marker policy bars at any weight.
queue_items.grounds: The rationale states that the English quotation closes at web:Isa.27.5 and calls it 'a translation-punctuation boundary carried here as non-driving corroboration alone'. web:Isa.27.5 ends with a closing curly double quote opened at web:Isa.27.2; that quotation span is WEB editorial punctuation (tier-4), and MT carries none of it — the row's own closing verse reads בַּיּ֖וֹם הַה֑וּא כֶּ֥רֶם חֶ֖מֶד עַנּוּ לָֽהּ (oshb:Isa.27.2, byte tier) at the row's opening verse, and the row's closing verse ends שָׁל֖וֹם יַֽעֲשֶׂה לִּֽי (oshb:Isa.27.5, byte tier) with no quotation apparatus of any kind. Tier-4 metadata is never boundary evidence and never corroboration; labelling it 'non-driving' does not license carrying it in the warrant.
queue_items.proposed_change: Strike the web:Isa.27.5 translation-punctuation sentence from boundary_rationale and let the rear edge stand on the oshb:Isa.27.6 onset alone; drop web:Isa.27.5 from boundary_evidence_refs if no non-tier-4 claim remains attached to it.

queue_items.claim: 'the book's one instance of a dedicated song-announcement formula' is an unswept uniqueness claim and is contradicted by the bytes at two further sites.
queue_items.grounds: The clause carries no digit-bearing sweep citation and names no swept object ('a dedicated song-announcement formula' is not a defined count object). Byte counterevidence: אָשִׁ֤ירָה נָּא֙ לִֽידִידִ֔י שִׁירַ֥ת דּוֹדִ֖י (oshb:Isa.5.1, byte tier) and שִׁ֤ירוּ לַֽיהוָה֙ שִׁ֣יר חָדָ֔שׁ (oshb:Isa.42.10, byte tier) are both first-person/imperative song announcements; the shir skeleton stands at 9 verses book-wide (sweep: 9 verses; oshb:Isa.3.19, oshb:Isa.5.1, oshb:Isa.23.15, oshb:Isa.23.16, oshb:Isa.24.9, oshb:Isa.26.1, oshb:Isa.30.29, oshb:Isa.42.10, oshb:Isa.53.9), a substring object that itself blends the necklace and rich-man tokens. The claim escaped the universals gate twice: 'one instance' is outside that detector's lexicon, and the sentence names a tier beside a ref, which trips its tier-vocabulary dampener.
queue_items.proposed_change: Replace with a swept, object-named statement (e.g. name the koh-yushar formula at יוּשַׁ֥ר הַשִּׁיר (oshb:Isa.26.1, byte tier) as ONE attested song-announcement form, with its digit), or delete the uniqueness clause; the construal disclaimer about the row's own verse stands without it.

queue_items.claim: The rear edge is argued as an address to Jacob and Israel; oshb:Isa.27.6 carries no address at all — it is third-person predication.
queue_items.grounds: The rationale reads that oshb:Isa.27.6 is 'addressing Jacob and Israel by name rather than continuing the vineyard's second-person/first-person address'. The verse's own bytes are הַבָּאִים֙ יַשְׁרֵ֣שׁ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב יָצִ֥יץ וּפָרַ֖ח יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Isa.27.6, byte tier): no vocative particle, no second-person form, the names standing as third-person subjects of third-masculine-singular verbs. The contrast term is also mis-set: inside oshb:Isa.27.2-Isa.27.5 the vineyard is never addressed in the second person either — it is carried by third-feminine-singular suffixes (אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ נֹֽצְרָ֔הּ, oshb:Isa.27.3, byte tier), while the one second-person form is the plural imperative עַנּוּ לָֽהּ (oshb:Isa.27.2, byte tier) addressed to an unnamed audience. The seam survives on a corrected warrant (referent/scene shift), but the stated form-class ground does not.
queue_items.proposed_change: Restate the rear-edge ground as a referent/scene shift — oshb:Isa.27.6 names Jacob and Israel as third-person subjects where oshb:Isa.27.2-Isa.27.5 carried a third-feminine-singular vineyard referent — and drop the word 'address' from both halves of the contrast.

The verse shifts at once to first-person divine speech, “I, Yahweh, am its keeper. I will water it every moment” (web:Isa.27.3), matching אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ נֹֽצְרָ֔הּ (oshb:Isa.27.3, byte tier). The English quotation closes at “Or else let him take hold of my strength, that he may make peace with me. Let him make peace with me.” (web:Isa.27.5), a translation-punctuation boundary carried here as non-driving corroboration alone; the byte-grounded edge is Isa.27.6's own onset, a bare participial form, הַבָּאִים֙ יַשְׁרֵ֣שׁ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב (oshb:Isa.27.6, byte tier), addressing Jacob and Israel by name rather than continuing the vineyard's second-person/first-person address.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: A single verse announces a cosmic judgment with its own ba-yom-hahu formula, “In that day, Yahweh… will punish leviathan, the fleeing serpent, and leviathan, the twisted serpent; and he will kill the dragon that is in the sea” (web:Isa.27.1), matching בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֡וּא יִפְקֹ֣ד יְהוָה֩ (oshb:Isa.27.1, byte tier) for the onset and עַ֤ל לִוְיָתָן֙ (oshb:Isa.27.1, byte tier), ‘upon Leviathan.’ A setumah (single-witness) follows this verse in the parashah layer, and the vineyard-song frame of Isa.27.2 opens a distinct, separately quoted unit. The onset formula itself, בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֡וּא (oshb:Isa.27.1, byte tier), recurs at exactly 3 verses book-wide at this same accented form (sweep: 3 verses); it does not by itself distinguish this verse from Isa.27.2, which opens the identical formula at accent_stripped tier (בַּיּ֖וֹם הַה֑וּא, oshb:Isa.27.2, byte tier in its own verse). What separates them is what follows the formula: here a complete verbal clause with its own divine subject, יִפְקֹ֣ד יְהוָה֩ (oshb:Isa.27.1, byte tier), while at Isa.27.2 the formula is followed first by a noun phrase, כֶּ֥רֶם חֶ֖מֶד (oshb:Isa.27.2, byte tier), opening a vineyard-summons that only completes across the following verses; the parashah layer marks the difference too, bracketing this verse alone with a setumah on both edges (after Isa.26.21 and after Isa.27.1), where the next closing mark after Isa.27.2 falls at Isa.27.6.

prev_row.device_notes: A setumah (single-witness) follows Isa.26.21, at the front seam of this row, and another follows Isa.27.1 itself, at its close — the parashah layer isolates this one-verse row on both edges. The verb יִפְקֹ֣ד (oshb:Isa.27.1, byte tier) recurs byte-identical at יִפְקֹ֣ד (oshb:Isa.27.3, byte tier; sweep: 2 verses book-wide), crossing this row's own closing edge; the two sites carry different speech-roles — the divine name is the visiting subject here, while at Isa.27.3 the speaker is the vineyard's keeper naming a different potential visitor — so the recurrence is disclosed as a lexical form and not read as a chain binding the row to Isa.27.3. The front-edge echo to לִפְקֹ֛ד (oshb:Isa.26.21, byte tier) links only at the shared three-consonant root, not at byte tier or at the whole-token skeleton — לִפְקֹ֛ד and יִפְקֹ֣ד are two distinct attested spellings of that root (sweep: 18 verses book-wide on the root).

next_row.boundary_rationale: A restoration promise opens on a bare participial onset, not a dated formula in the bytes themselves — “In days to come, Jacob will take root. Israel will blossom and bud” (web:Isa.27.6) renders the dating sense, but the Hebrew reads הַבָּאִים֙ יַשְׁרֵ֣שׁ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב (oshb:Isa.27.6, byte tier), a bare participle supplying no noun of its own; the dating gloss is the rendering's contribution. The argument continues through Isa.27.7's third-masculine-singular suffixes and Isa.27.8's third-feminine-singular suffixes, both read as referring back to Jacob and Israel of Isa.27.6 though carried by two different suffix classes rather than one repeated pronoun, through the atonement clause “the iniquity of Jacob will be forgiven” (web:Isa.27.9), matching יְכֻפַּ֣ר עֲוֺֽן יַעֲקֹ֔ב (oshb:Isa.27.9, byte tier), and on to a contrastive judgment on an unnamed fortified city (web:Isa.27.10, web:Isa.27.11) offered as a foil to Jacob's own measured discipline. Isa.27.12 opens its own ba-yom-hahu formula, a fresh frame this row does not share.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A finer split at Isa.27.6 alone, corroborated by a single-witness setumah recorded there, was considered but rejected. Isa.27.7 opens not with a pronoun but with an interrogative-comparative construction, and its suffixes are third-masculine-singular, מַכֵּ֖הוּ הִכָּ֑הוּ (oshb:Isa.27.7, byte tier; the suffix class held as a byte-checkable claim, no morphology layer being staged); the referential link back to Jacob and Israel of Isa.27.6 is arguable from those 3ms forms, but Isa.27.8 shifts to third-feminine-singular suffixes instead, בְּשַׁלְחָ֣הּ תְּרִיבֶ֑נָּה (oshb:Isa.27.8, byte tier), a different suffix class rather than a continuation of the same one; the two verses are bound to Isa.27.6 by argument, not by one pronoun carried across all three.

next_row.boundary_rationale: A single verse carries its own ba-yom-hahu onset, “It will happen in that day that Yahweh will thresh from the flowing stream of the Euphrates to the brook of Egypt” (web:Isa.27.12), matching וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יַחְבֹּ֧ט יְהוָ֛ה (oshb:Isa.27.12, byte tier). The onset is the waw-prefixed long form of the formula, distinct from the book's bare form; at skeleton tier it stands at 13 verses book-wide (sweep: 13 verses). Isa.27.13 opens a second, independent instance of the same formula with a different image (trumpet rather than threshing), so the repeated onset is read as two proclamations rather than one unit spanning both verses; a setumah (single-witness) separates the two in the parashah layer.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging Isa.27.12 and Isa.27.13 into one ingathering row was considered, since both share the same destination image, but rejected: the two onsets agree only at accent_stripped tier — וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא (oshb:Isa.27.12, byte tier) and וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.27.13, byte tier) differ from each other in their accents — and each introduces a distinct image, threshing against the trumpet, with a single-witness setumah recorded after oshb:Isa.27.12 (tier-3, non-driving) standing between the two. The waw prefixed on both onsets is a sequencing form and could as readily support reading the pair as one continuing announcement; that rival is weighed and set aside because both halves are complete on their own terms and the mark, however weak, falls exactly at the image change.

next_row.boundary_rationale: This span opens on the ה֗וֹי exclamation that opens the chapter (oshb:Isa.28.1, byte tier), pronounced over “the crown of pride of the drunkards of Ephraim” (web:Isa.28.1). The echo at “The crown of pride of the drunkards of Ephraim will be trodden under foot.” (web:Isa.28.3) reuses עֲטֶ֤רֶת גֵּאוּת֙ / עֲטֶ֥רֶת גֵּא֖וּת at the accent-stripped tier (oshb:Isa.28.1, oshb:Isa.28.3), while the surrounding drunkard-noun spelling shifts between the two verses, a plene/defective pair the row does not smooth over. The reversal at Isa.28.5 turns on לַעֲטֶ֣רֶת צְבִ֔י (oshb:Isa.28.5, byte tier), “a crown of glory” (web:Isa.28.5) — the third of exactly 3 sites of this crown noun in the chapter and 4 book-wide (sweep: 4 verses at skeleton tier) — set over לִשְׁאָ֖ר עַמּֽוֹ (oshb:Isa.28.5, byte tier), the bare noun member of the book's four-way remnant family, “the residue of his people” (web:Isa.28.5); this keeps the same crown motif running rather than opening a separate address, so the row holds Isa.28.5-Isa.28.6 inside the complex instead of cutting a short reversal there. The priest-and-prophet turn at Isa.28.7 keeps the same speaking voice, so the row continues through the mockery of the teaching method quoted at “Whom will he teach knowledge?” (web:Isa.28.9) and the announced judgment by a foreign tongue, closing on “fall backward, be broken, be snared, and be taken.” (web:Isa.28.13) -- the verse just before the imperative address that opens a fresh addressee at web:Isa.28.14.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: The stronger rival opens on the day-formula בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.28.5, byte tier) — the same bare verse-initial formula that opens unit divisions at Isa.27.1 and Isa.27.2, and in its waw-prefixed long form at Isa.27.12 and Isa.27.13 — while the parashah layer records a setumah after MT 28:4 and another after MT 28:6 (tier-3, single-witness, non-driving), bracketing precisely the Isa.28.5-Isa.28.6 pair the rival would cut loose. The pair is kept in nonetheless: the crown noun's third in-chapter site at Isa.28.5 continues the same figure opened at Isa.28.1 and Isa.28.3 rather than starting a fresh image, and the same speaking voice carries through the priest-and-prophet material that follows.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: The closing verse of the book-level parent grouping opens with its own repetition of the day-formula, “It will happen in that day that a great trumpet will be blown” (web:Isa.27.13), matching וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.27.13, byte tier) for the onset and יִתָּקַע֮ בְּשׁוֹפָ֣ר גָּדוֹל֒ (oshb:Isa.27.13, byte tier), ‘a great trumpet will be blown,’ and resolves in worship at Jerusalem, “they will worship Yahweh in the holy mountain at Jerusalem” (web:Isa.27.13). The verse is the closing verse of its book-level parent grouping, which corroborates this row's own close; the seam itself is carried in the bytes on the far side too — Isa.28.1 opens with its own verse-initial woe onset, ה֗וֹי (oshb:Isa.28.1, byte tier), a member of the book's wider woe-series inventory and the start of a fresh series, distinct in kind from this row's own day-formula-and-trumpet onset.

next_row.boundary_rationale: A fresh addressee opens this row: לָכֵ֛ן שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אַנְשֵׁ֣י לָצ֑וֹן (oshb:Isa.28.14, byte tier), “Therefore hear Yahweh’s word, you scoffers, that rule this people in Jerusalem:” (web:Isa.28.14), the summons formula standing at 3 verses book-wide at skeleton tier (sweep: 3 verses). The particle argues the reply rhetorically from what precedes — the precept-on-precept mockery of Isa.28.9-Isa.28.13 supplies its premise — but the clause itself is a fresh second-person-plural imperative summons naming a new addressee, Jerusalem's ruling scoffers rather than Ephraim's drunkards, and it is that addressee shift and imperative onset, not the connector's backward reach, that opens the row here and closes off the drunkard complex ending at web:Isa.28.13. The koh-amar frame at לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Isa.28.16, byte tier) opens the divine reply “Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious cornerstone of a sure foundation.” (web:Isa.28.16), which the row keeps together with the covenant-with-death accusation it answers rather than treating the cornerstone saying as its own unit, since the same addressee and frame carry through. The row closes on the oracle-report formula “I have heard a decree of destruction from the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, on the whole earth.” (web:Isa.28.22), the verse just before a fresh imperative-summons onset at web:Isa.28.23.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival cut would open a fresh row at לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Isa.28.16, byte tier), the divine-frame formula answering the covenant-with-death quotation of Isa.28.15, rather than at the imperative address that opens the unit at Isa.28.14; it is rejected because the addressee and frame carry through from Isa.28.14 into the cornerstone saying without a fresh vocative or scene change.
